_comment: Service pairs: the Compose service and the chart component that runs the
same application. The parity gate (scripts/config-parity-check.py) compares
the environment both surfaces give that application.
Three categories, per service. Every entry carries the reason it is one —
an entry without a reason is a gap in disguise.
mayDiffer    : the chart sets the variable and its value is the
Kubernetes one — an address, a topology fact, or a
deliberate policy difference. The variable must still be
present: the application needs it on both surfaces.
composeOnly  : the variable only makes sense on the Compose surface.
notRead      : no code in the repository reads the variable.
A variable in none of the three must be configured the same way on both
surfaces — that is the parity this gate protects.

mayDiffer.ARANGO_DB: the chart's ArangoDB instance serves _system, ArangoDB's own database, which always exists; Compose uses a dedicated genie-ai database. Intentional divergence: moving an existing deployment means migrating every collection, not switching a value. The knob is data.arangodb.database (default _system)
mayDiffer.ARANGO_URL: in-cluster Service DNS instead of the Compose service name
mayDiffer.ARANGO_PASSWORD: carried by the arango-root-secret Secret the operator provides
mayDiffer.ENABLE_OBSERVABILITY: the chart's observability tier is an operator-enabled install of its own; Compose gates the same services behind a profile
mayDiffer.KEYCLOAK_URL: the backend resolves JWKS in-cluster; Compose reaches Keycloak through the public origin
mayDiffer.OPEA_HOST: in-cluster Service DNS instead of the Compose service name
mayDiffer.OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: the collector is an operator-managed instance with its own Service name
mayDiffer.TRANSLATION_BACKEND: the chart names a translation API, and the application treats a named API as mandatory; Compose leaves the choice to the startup probe
mayDiffer.TRANSLATION_CACHE_HOST: in-cluster Service DNS instead of the Compose service name
mayDiffer.VICTORIALOGS_URL: the collector is an operator-managed instance with its own Service name
mayDiffer.VLLM_API_KEY: carried by the vllm-api-key Secret the operator provides
mayDiffer.VLLM_TRANSLATION_ENDPOINT: the chart points at the OPEA tier's endpoint (in-cluster Service or GPU node); Compose at its own guardrail service
mayDiffer.CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: same allowlist intent, expressed with the deployment's public origin (ingress.host) instead of Compose's localhost list
mayDiffer.CSP_CONNECT_SRC: same policy intent, expressed with the deployment's public origin
mayDiffer.GPU_NODE_HOST: the chart names the GPU node it was configured with; Compose leaves it empty unless the remote-GPU topology is used
mayDiffer.OKF_ENABLED: the flag follows the tier gate: the parity render switches the tier on (--set okf.enabled=true) so its rows get compared, while the Compose reference ships dark (OKF_ENABLED=0). A production deployment chooses the value on both surfaces; the gate compares them at opposite states by construction

notRead.EMAIL_FROM: read by no service in the repository — the Keycloak convergence job is the only consumer of the EMAIL_* names, and it takes the password from a Secret
notRead.EMAIL_HOST: read by no service in the repository — see EMAIL_FROM
notRead.EMAIL_PORT: read by no service in the repository — see EMAIL_FROM
notRead.EMAIL_SECURE: read by no service in the repository — see EMAIL_FROM
notRead.EMAIL_USER: read by no service in the repository — see EMAIL_FROM
notRead.EMAIL_PASSWORD: read by no service in the repository — see EMAIL_FROM

codeDefault.KEYCLOAK_ADDITIONAL_REALMS: empty in Compose; the backend parses an unset value as an empty JSON array, so leaving it unset is the same result
codeDefault.OPEA_SSL_SKIP_VERIFY: empty in Compose; the code treats an unset value as 'verify', and the chart's NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=1 says the same thing for the Node client
codeDefault.KEYCLOAK_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS: the shared OIDC verifier applies its own 5000ms discovery budget when the variable is unset, and Compose leaves it unset too — both surfaces run the same default
codeDefault.KEYCLOAK_EXPECTED_ISSUER: the variable pins a strict issuer only when set; on this service it is unset on both surfaces, so the verifier accepts the discovery issuer plus the KEYCLOAK_PUBLIC_URL / KEYCLOAK_BROWSER_ISSUER aliases
codeDefault.KEYCLOAK_DISCOVERY_URL: Compose leaves it empty and the shared verifier falls back to KEYCLOAK_URL, which the chart sets to the in-cluster Keycloak Service. The realm's hostname is PINNED to the public origin, so the discovery document fetched in-cluster publishes the PUBLIC issuer: the browser's tokens and the verifier's document agree without an alias. A deployment whose discovery host must differ from KEYCLOAK_URL sets it through the service's `env` map (services.<service>.env).

KEYCLOAK_PROXY_CLIENT_SECRET.why: carried by the keycloak-proxy-client-secret Secret through envFrom; the operator provides the key, so there is no value to compare

TRANSLATION_CACHE_PASSWORD.why: carried by the translation-cache-password Secret through envFrom; the operator provides the key, so there is no value to compare

composeOnly.AGENT_ENABLED: the chart does not deploy the agent-service tier yet (the compose-side agentic branch, story 2.4): the backend's routing helper reads the flag once and parks the branch unless it is exactly '1', so its absence on the chart IS the dark state, not a gap. The entry moves to mayDiffer/both surfaces when the tier lands on the chart.
composeOnly.AGENT_SERVICE_URL: the chart does not deploy the agent-service tier yet — there is no in-cluster endpoint to name; the Compose value is the compose service name. Same re-entry as AGENT_ENABLED when the tier lands.
composeOnly.AGENT_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS: sizes the agent leg (POST /v1/runs) that the chart does not run yet — the pair rule lives in docs/agent-budget-deadline-pairs.md and the knob becomes a chart value when the tier is deployed by the chart.
composeOnly.AGENT_TRANSLATION_MAX_TOKENS: the agentic-path translation-leg allowances: read fail-closed by the BFF's agentic translation leg (story 2.10, AD-14), and no deployed surface serves that leg yet — the chart does not install the agentic request path (the agent service itself is unpaired for the same reason). Wiring the knobs into the chart backend is the deployment story's surface (the deferral is filed in _bmad-output deferred-work), and a knob wired before its consumer would be configuration theatre on the chart surface.
composeOnly.AGENT_TRANSLATION_MAX_CALLS: the agentic-path translation-leg allowances: read fail-closed by the BFF's agentic translation leg (story 2.10, AD-14), and no deployed surface serves that leg yet — the chart does not install the agentic request path (the agent service itself is unpaired for the same reason). mayDiffer.CLAMSCAN_PORT: the chart dials the clamav Service's port (services.clamav.port, 3310); Compose leaves it empty and the application talks to the embedded daemon on its default port.
mayDiffer.VIRUS_SCANNING: the chart ships the ClamAV tier and turns the scan step on; Compose leaves the flag to the operator, whose default deployment runs without it.
mayDiffer.CLAMSCAN_LOCAL_FALLBACK: the chart states the fallback OFF (services.documentRepository.clamavLocalFallback): the scanner is the clamav Deployment and the doc-repo pod's embedded daemon stays down, so a local fallback would find nothing. Compose leaves it unset and the embedded daemon IS the scanner, so the fallback is on there.

composeOnly.LLM_SERVER_HOST_IP: Compose points these at its own vllm service name; the chart configures the endpoint form instead (VLLM_LLM_ENDPOINT), which the code parses into host and port before reading either variable, so leaving them unset yields the same endpoint. The chart never sets the name: the code derives the endpoint from the configured GPU endpoint (the parsed hostname overrides this fallback), so the compose service name only ever made sense on that surface.
composeOnly.LLM_SERVER_PORT: Compose points these at its own vllm service name; the chart configures the endpoint form instead (VLLM_LLM_ENDPOINT), which the code parses into host and port before reading either variable, so leaving them unset yields the same endpoint. The chart never sets the name: the code derives the endpoint from the configured GPU endpoint (the parsed hostname overrides this fallback), so the compose service name only ever made sense on that surface.
composeOnly.EMBEDDING_BACKEND: the ROCm GPU-tier backend switch, and it has to be the SAME variable the corpus and retrieval legs use: the query encoder must embed with the same model the corpus was embedded with, or the query vector and the document vectors are not comparable (dataprep + retriever move together for the same reason). It only points somewhere on a deployment that runs the compose profile-pooled vLLM embedding instance (docker-compose.yaml `rocm-models`, vllm-embedding); on the chart the TEI service is the serving backend and there is no in-cluster pooling Service to point at. The ROCm k8s profile is deferred by docs/helm-k8s-rocm-handoff.md (§Task-14 addendum), which prescribes landing the four-workload chart shape WITH these switches, not before
composeOnly.EMBEDDING_VLLM_ENDPOINT: the address of the compose-overlay vLLM embedding instance; no in-cluster Service of that name exists until the deferred ROCm chart profile lands (docs/helm-k8s-rocm-handoff.md §Task-14 addendum)
composeOnly.MODEL_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: the shared embedding HTTP budget that ships with the GPU embedding backend: Compose restates the code default (600, core/model_http_policy.py) so an operator tuning the GPU-tier budget can see and move it; the chart omits the row, which resolves through the same code default — identical behavior on both surfaces, documented difference
composeOnly.VLLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL_ID: the model name the compose-overlay embedding instance serves (paired with its --served-model-name); meaningless until that instance exists in-cluster — deferred with the ROCm chart profile (docs/helm-k8s-rocm-handoff.md §Task-14 addendum)

OPENAI_API_KEY.why: Compose maps `${VLLM_API_KEY:-}` into it (docker-compose.yaml); the chart delivers the same GPU key from the vllm-api-key Secret under that name — the translation and condense clients read only OPENAI_API_KEY for their Bearer header, and a GPU node enforcing the key would see 'Bearer None' without it.

composeOnly.PORT: The chart does not set the name at all: its Deployment carries the port as containerPort 8090 (services.frontend.port), and the frontend image's embedded nginx listens on that baked-in default — the PORT env only steers the compose-run process.

mayDiffer.ARANGO_DB: the chart's ArangoDB instance serves _system, ArangoDB's own database, which always exists; Compose uses a dedicated genie-ai database — the same adaptation the backend, dataprep and retriever entries carry

mayDiffer.KEYCLOAK_URL: the chart derives the public edge address from ingress.scheme + ingress.host (the same derivation the convergence Job's KC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN uses); Compose assembles it from the NGINX host/port variables
mayDiffer.OKF_RAGAS_SERVE_URL: the chart's chatqna Service is named chatqna; Compose's container is chatqna-xeon-backend-server — same application, either surface's own DNS
mayDiffer.RAGAS_JUDGE_BASE_URL: the chart derives the LLM endpoint from the OPEA GPU tier (external nodeHost or the in-cluster service); Compose points at its own vllm container
mayDiffer.TEI_EMBED_HOST: the chart derives the embedding endpoint from the OPEA GPU tier (external nodeHost or the in-cluster service); Compose names its own TEI container — a name that exists on neither Kubernetes surface, so the derived address is the only live one here

codeDefault.KEYCLOAK_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS: the shared OIDC verifier applies its own 5000ms discovery budget when the variable is unset, and Compose leaves it unset too — both surfaces run the same default
codeDefault.KEYCLOAK_EXPECTED_ISSUER: the variable pins a strict issuer only when set; on this service it is unset on both surfaces, so the verifier accepts the discovery issuer plus the KEYCLOAK_PUBLIC_URL / KEYCLOAK_BROWSER_ISSUER aliases
codeDefault.KEYCLOAK_DISCOVERY_URL: Compose leaves it empty and the shared verifier falls back to KEYCLOAK_URL, which the chart sets to the in-cluster Keycloak Service. The realm's hostname is PINNED to the public origin, so the discovery document fetched in-cluster publishes the PUBLIC issuer: the browser's tokens and the verifier's document agree without an alias. A deployment whose discovery host must differ from KEYCLOAK_URL sets it through the service's `env` map (services.<service>.env).

unpaired.chatqna-xeon-ui-server: the OPEA demo UI is not deployed by the chart

unpaired.grafana: the chart's Grafana is a grafana-operator custom resource, configured through the CR
unpaired.guardrail: the chart deploys no guardrail; the orchestrators tolerate an unreachable one and carry its default address

unpaired.postgres-init: the chart's PostgreSQL is CloudNativePG; the operator creates the database and its owner

unpaired.arango-vector-db-init: one-shot chown of the ArangoDB data volumes to uid 999 — the chart's ArangoDB is a kube-arangodb operator custom resource whose storage the operator owns; there is no chart-side container to pair
unpaired.backend-init: one-shot chown of the backend volumes (data, Uploads, database_backups) to uid 1000 for the compose non-root posture (#1227) — the chart grants the same write access with fsGroup on the pod, which the kubelet applies at mount time; there is no init service to pair
unpaired.document-repository-init: one-shot chown of the uploads volume to uid 1000 (#1227) — same as backend-init, the chart covers it with fsGroup on the pod
unpaired.secrets-ssl-init: one-shot re-permission of the host ./secrets/ssl tree to root:101 for the gid-101 nginx edge — the chart's edge is Envoy Gateway with cert-manager TLS; there is no ssl tree and no nginx to own it
unpaired.victorialogs-init: one-shot chown of the VictoriaLogs data volume to uid 65534 — the chart's log store is a vmoperator VMSingle custom resource whose storage the operator owns
unpaired.vllm-embedding: the ROCm GPU-tier's fourth vLLM instance (pooling for the bge-large-en-v1.5 embedder on gfx1151, where the TEI image cannot run); Compose gates it behind the `rocm-models` profile, so it is absent from the NVIDIA render entirely. The chart deploys the OPEA tier's embedding model through values (paired as `tei`/`textgen`-style Deployments) and carries no ROCm pooling variant — deferred with the ROCm chart profile (docs/helm-k8s-rocm-handoff.md §Task-14 addendum)
unpaired.vllm-reranker: the ROCm GPU-tier's vLLM reranker instance (serving bge-reranker-v2-m3 as a Cohere-shaped /v1/rerank on gfx1151, where the TEI image cannot run); Compose gates it behind the `rocm-models` profile, so it is absent from the NVIDIA render entirely. The chart's reranking model is the OPEA tier's TEI Deployment (paired as `tei_reranker`) and carries no ROCm pooling variant — deferred with the ROCm chart profile (docs/helm-k8s-rocm-handoff.md §Task-14 addendum)
unpaired.searxng: the chart does not install SearXNG — the agent's web-search meta-search backend is delivered on the Compose/ansible surface only, its adoption on k3s is operator-owned (AR-10), with the same flag semantics; the Compose service ships dark behind AGENT_WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED
